plan: This auction structure mirrors a second-price (Vickrey) auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. In such mechanisms, bidding truthfully (equal to your value) is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth; bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. Since my value is $28, I will bid exactly that.

This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price (Vickrey) auction: my sealed bid sets my exit price, and the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, truthful bidding is a dominant strategy—bidding above value risks overpaying, bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Since I have no history to suggest otherwise and this is a one-shot game, the optimal action is to bid exactly my private value of $23 to maximize expected profit.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the clock stops at the second-highest sealed bid, determining the price), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.
